title: Nasruddin and the Ferry (The Language of Life)
summary: During a stormy river crossing, a scholar rebuked Nasruddin for not knowing formal Persian rhetoric: "Half your life is wasted!"...
full_text:
During a stormy river crossing, a scholar rebuked Nasruddin for not knowing formal Persian rhetoric: "Half your life is wasted!"

When the boat sprung a leak, Nasruddin asked: "Do you know how to swim?"
"No!" wept the scholar.

"Then your whole life is wasted!" cried Nasruddin, jumping into the waves. "For grammar cannot keep a sinking man afloat!"
moral: Bookish pride drowns in deep water; living wisdom knows how to swim.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Nasruddin and the Ferry"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
